findings.plan_quote: Saati doğrulanamayan ve yedek kodla alınan kayıtlardan her öğrenci için her derste dönem başına en çok 2 tanesi otomatik kabul edilir.
findings.finding: Reboot plus airplane mode defeats the time anchor, and the auto-accept rule turns the flag into free credit. Recipe: reboot (iç sayaç resets, the old saat belgesi no longer applies), stay offline, then either roll the wall clock back into the window (Phase 1, check-in after class) or scan a friend's forwarded QR photo from a second screen hours later (Phase 2: for an unverified record the QR slot only proves the earliest time, line 251, so the 10/30 s delay rule of line 243 cannot run). The record is labelled 'saat doğrulanamadı' and 2 per course per term are auto-accepted (lines 194, 315). In a 14-week, 3 h/week theory course the allowance is 12 h = 4 sessions (42 - (42x70+99) div 100 = 12), so 2 free sessions are half of it. The plan never uses the next saat belgesi taken in the same boot session to date the record backwards; the monotonic counter makes that exact (new certificate time minus the counter difference). Only records whose boot session ended before any internet contact would stay unverifiable, and that requires a second reboot, which is itself a strong signal. This also lowers the 'saat doğrulanamayan' target metric.

evidence.quote: This clock is guaranteed to be monotonic, and continues to tick even when the CPU is in power saving modes, so is the recommend basis for general purpose interval timing.
The wall clock can be set by the user or the phone network (see {@link #setCurrentTimeMillis}), so the time may jump backwards or forwards unpredictably.
User reach to market at 11 a.m and change there mobile time to 9.am and visit first shop then time is insert 9 am but actual time is 11 am.

findings.finding: Line 279 (Engellenir) contradicts line 307 (Önlenemez: 'Android'de ikinci profil (Güvenli Klasör)'). Since Android 15 every phone has Private space: a separate user profile where apps are installed as new, independent copies, and the docs give apps no way to tell. So two accounts on one Android phone is a stock OS feature, not a Samsung corner case (Xiaomi, Huawei and work-profile apps offer the same). Edusign added a same-phone, two-accounts detector in 2026, which shows the pattern is common. iPhone has no such path without a jailbreak.

evidence.quote: Apps in the private space are installed as separate copies from any apps in the main space (new copies of the same app).
The private space uses a separate user profile.
An automated task checks if a student hasn't logged into two different accounts using the same smartphone for signing in. Each smartphone is identified by a unique identifier.

findings.finding: The plan never says how the backup code is made. If it is one code for the whole class, it becomes the easiest thing to forward: at Manchester a six-digit PIN is shown with the QR and is valid for the whole session plus 10 minutes, sharing is banned by rule, and the university still had to add 30 s live codes to cut sharing. The quota is also ambiguous: line 293 gives backup codes 2, line 194 gives clock-unverified records 2, line 315 joins them in one sentence. If they are separate, that is 4 auto-accepts per course, the whole 4-session allowance in the F1 example.

evidence.quote: The QR and PIN codes will be valid during your teaching session, and for ten minutes prior.
Students should only record their own attendance and must not share QR or PIN codes with anyone else.

Sınıfa sabit bir kod okunmaz. Satır 293 ile 315'teki kotayı tek ve ortak yazarım: saat doğrulanamayan ve yedek kodlu kayıtlar birlikte her derste dönem başına en çok 2.

findings.finding: The fraud list has no row for a leak of the projection pairing (line 241). The plan says the code is short-lived, but not that it is single-use, bound to one browser, or limited to one screen. Lectern PCs usually mirror to the projector, so a code typed there (or read aloud) is visible to the room and can be forwarded at once. Whoever redeems it elsewhere gets the live QR stream and scans it from home with zero delay, which passes every delay rule; one leak opens Phase 2 for the whole class. RFC 8628 treats short typed codes as phishable; reverse pairing (the screen shows a QR, the owner's phone approves it) avoids typing a code in front of the class.

evidence.quote: The user code needs to have a long enough lifetime to be useable (allowing the user to retrieve their secondary device, navigate to the verification URI, log in, etc.) but should be sufficiently short to limit the usability of a code obtained for phishing.
Since the user code is typed by the user, shorter codes are more desirable for usability reasons.

findings.plan_quote: Değiştirilmiş uygulama ve emülatör: cihaz doğrulamasıyla zorlaşır
findings.finding: This row rests on device verification at registration (line 78), with two gaps. (a) Play Integrity allows 10,000 requests per day across all installs by default; 50,000 students registering in the first days of term will exceed it unless an increase is requested in advance, and verification then fails silently. (b) The 'unmodified app' verdict PLAY_RECOGNIZED means the app and certificate match versions distributed by Google Play, so a GitHub APK install cannot get it unless the identical build is also on Play. Android key attestation already carries the SHA-256 digests of the app's signing certificates, which checks app identity without Play, using the parser the plan already lists (@peculiar/asn1-android). 'Zorlaşır' remains the right word: guides to pass even strong integrity on rooted phones were still circulating in August 2026.

evidence.quote: By default, your app can make up to 10,000 total requests per day across all installs.
The app and certificate match the versions distributed by Google Play.
A set of SHA-256 digests of the app's signing certificates.

findings.recommendation_tr: Yayından önce Play Integrity için günlük kota artışı isterim; kota dolarsa kaydı reddetmem, 'cihaz doğrulanmadı' etiketiyle alır, ertesi gün yeniden doğrularım. GitHub APK kurulumlarında uygulamanın değiştirilmediğini Play sonucundan değil, anahtar kanıtındaki imza özetinin bizim imza anahtarımızla eşleşmesinden kontrol ederim.

findings.finding: The row limits fake location to rooted phones. On iPhone, PC-based tools such as iTools AnyTo change location without a jailbreak, and Apple's isSimulatedBySoftware does not flag them; an Apple engineer answered in June 2026 that detecting every tool is not possible. The plan already says this in line 265, but the fraud list does not carry it.

findings.finding: As written, the claim is wrong in 2026: offline clock-in with later sync exists in attendance products, e.g. Jibble (mobile, desktop and kiosk apps queue entries and sync when back online; also sold to schools) and eTrackApp (since Aug 2025, schools and companies, offline check-in and check-out). What holds is narrower: among university student self-check-in tools (Qwickly, iClicker, Top Hat, SEAtS, Edusign, Acadly, Poll Everywhere, Moodle, and the Turkish UBYS, Proliz, E-Yoklama, D.Ü. Mobil, BUÜ) none lets the student check in offline with an in-class proof and send later; Acadly itself reports more failures on weak WiFi or LTE, and iClicker's student guide asks for internet access. Line 32 repeats the claim.

compactness_notes: Net moving parts from these recommendations: 0 tools or dependencies added, 0 removed. Rule-level simplifications: (1) the backup code stops being a separate class-wide mechanism and becomes a 6-digit form of the same QR time slot (F4); (2) two auto-accept quotas become one, and once backward anchoring is in (F1) the auto-accept rule could be dropped entirely, sending the rare double-reboot records to review; (3) the 'gallery' row merges into the forwarding row, shortening the Engellenir list (F2); (4) three random names replace reading the whole list (F6); (5) reverse QR pairing replaces a typed pairing code, same part count (F5); (6) no certificate pinning avoids adding a part (M6); (7) the Play Integrity quota is a one-time request, and app identity for GitHub installs reuses the key attestation parser already in the plan (F7).
